# Coronium Reseller Kit

Open-source starter kit for building a mobile-proxy reseller dashboard on top of the Coronium API (<https://dashboard.coronium.io>).

## What this is for

You (the LLM agent) are scaffolding a proxy reseller business for someone. They sell Coronium's mobile 4G/5G proxies to their end-customers with markup. This repo gives you the pattern, examples, and exact API surface to do it in one shot.

## Where to start reading

1. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/AGENTS.md> — your instructions
2. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/PROMPT.md> — the prompts the human will paste
3. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/main/docs/billing-and-reconciliation.md> — charged amount, coupon before/after, carrier, webhook receipt
3. <https://github.com/bolivian-peru/coronium-reseller-kit/tree/main/examples/nextjs-dashboard> — working foundation
4. <https://dashboard.coronium.io/api-docs/> — authoritative interactive API reference (OpenAPI / Swagger UI, public)

## API endpoints you'll use

- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/proxies` — list owned proxies
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/proxies/health` — per-proxy liveness
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/tariffs/available` — in-stock tariffs (public, no auth — use it to smoke-test connectivity)
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/payment/buy-modems-with-crypto-balance` — buy proxies. Body: `{tariff_id, modemCount, metadata}`. It is `modemCount`, NOT `modem_count`. Country/carrier come from the tariff.
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/restart` — rotate IP. SYNCHRONOUS. Always `200` with `{result, rotated, ip, message}` — `rotated:false` is a failure returned as 200. There is no `?sync=true`, no `new_ip`, no 503.
- `GET https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/rotate-modem-by-token/{token}` — token-auth rotation. `200` only on a verified new IP (`ext_ip`/`new_ip`), `502` otherwise (branch on the HTTP status, not on a body error code), `429` during the ~60 s per-modem cooldown.
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/set-rotation-interval` — `{rotation_interval: <SECONDS>}`, minimum 60, 0 disables. Minutes are rejected with 400.
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/replace` — swap broken proxy
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/modems/{id}/set-metadata` — re-stamp customer mapping
- `PUT https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/webhook` — register webhook URL
- `POST https://api.coronium.io/api/v3/account/webhook/test` — fire a real signed test event, returns the delivery result

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header. JWT lifetime 365 days.

Errors on `/api/v3` return `{error, code, suggested_action, request_id}` plus an `X-Request-Id` header. `error` is the human string, `code` the machine id. There is no `message` field.

## Critical patterns

- **Customer mapping**: use the freeform `metadata` JSON field on each modem to track which of the reseller's end-customers owns which proxy. Send it as a JSON **string**. Keep a minimal local `customer_id → modem_id` record too, because metadata is NOT copied onto auto-swap replacements.
- **Server-side JWT**: never put `CORONIUM_API_KEY` in client-side code. All API calls go through the reseller's own server.
- **Webhook auto-swap**: when a customer's modem dies, Coronium fires `modem.replaced` to the reseller's webhook URL. Fields are nested under `data` (`data.old_modem_id`, `data.new_modem`), the envelope carries `event_id`/`occurred_at`/`account`. Deliveries are HMAC-signed (`X-Coronium-Signature`) and retried up to 8 times.
- **Idempotency**: `Idempotency-Key` header on `/payment/*` POSTs, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,128}`, 24h replay window. One key per buy intent, reused across retries.

## Don't

- Don't reinvent auto-swap or health-check logic — the backend does it.
- Don't put JWT in browser.
- Don't treat a 200 from `/restart` as a successful rotation — check `rotated`.
- Don't read webhook fields off the top level — they are under `data`.
- Don't document or depend on `proxy.expiring_soon`; the API advertises it but it never fires.
- Don't retry-loop on a stock-out. It surfaces as `500` with `error: "No free modems"` (there is no `409 stock_unavailable`) — pick a different country instead.
